verdicts.note: 'Serve the people, not the bureaucracy' and 'responsible stewardship of taxpayer dollars' on his site [S4], repeated from the primary statement [S1]. That is a stated restraint posture, not an endorsement inference, so -1 at medium holds. Without specific cuts it should not go higher.

Affiliation inference. The dossier says no housing proposal was found on his site (line 69). The basis is his development-industry career and the Master Builders, realtors and Affordable Housing Council endorsements [S4][S5]; none of these is a stated housing position. The primary statement's 'business-minded approach to housing costs' [S1] gives no mechanism and no direction on the market-vs-public axis.

His 'not running to be a career politician' line [S4] is outsider framing, but his profile is institutional: Planning Commission chair confirmed by the council [S2], Charter Review commissioner [S3], and seats on the Agricultural Advisory, Transportation and Conservation Futures bodies [S4]. He is also endorsed by the outgoing District 1 incumbent and the former County Executive [S5]. The two directions cancel, so 0 (genuinely mixed) fits better than +1 at medium.

S4 is her own signed questionnaire (signed 'under penalty of perjury' 04/05/2026; checked in the cached copy), not an affiliation inference. She answered yes to progressive taxes as wealth increases and yes to raising developer impact fees. These are yes/no answers to the questioner's own wording, so medium is right; high would overstate them.

She wants more infrastructure money for unincorporated areas, new rural bus service and more funding for mobile outreach and for community colleges serving unhoused students [S4][S6]. Her free-text answers place her consistently toward investment.

She answered yes to 'robust investment in publicly owned housing/subsidized housing' and proposes rent subsidies [S4]. That outweighs the supply tools she also lists (density, accessory-unit incentives) [S6], so +1 rather than +2.

Her only free-text safety answer is about structural oversight of the sheriff, plus rural mobile outreach as a homelessness response [S4]. Neither is a direct position on enforcement or staffing, and the yes on firearms regulation is not on this axis. Low confidence is honest; keep it.
She answered yes to local climate investments, and her own free-text answer lists climate action 'in partnership with the communities that are impacted the most' [S4]. Medium is supported.

She has never served on the council, completed Emerge candidate training, argues for 'diversity of representation' and new candidates bringing 'a new perspective,' and was elected only to the Charter Review Commission [S4][S5]. Her establishment endorsements [S7] are endorsements, not a record. +1 at medium is supported.
